terms.definition: The distance traveled per unit of time — distance divided by time.
terms.function: Tells how fast an object moves without any direction information.
terms.whereItIs: Read on the track as meters per second while the car rolls.
terms.whyItMatters: It is the most used physics ratio and the basis of speedometers.

terms.definition: Total distance traveled divided by total time elapsed, across a whole journey.
terms.whyItMatters: It flattens stops and bursts into one trip-level number — the easy one to compute with a stopwatch.
terms.whereItIs: The final reading of the distance ticker after a run.

terms.definition: The speed at one particular moment — what a speedometer needle shows.
terms.whyItMatters: Explains why a vehicle can break a speed limit even when its average over a mile is right.
terms.whereItIs: The live m/s readout on the car while it moves.

terms.definition: A graph with distance on one axis and time on the other; its slope equals speed.
terms.whyItMatters: Reading the slope gives speed at a glance; a flat line means the object is stopped.
terms.whereItIs: The floating screen above the track drawing the car's distance history.
